counterfactual_missing_items: No clear evidence of capillary malformations
decisive_items: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant
The patient used a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
response.rationale: The presence of a KRIT1 variant and a history of intracranial hemorrhage strongly support the diagnosis of cerebral cavernous malformations.

rejected.why: Lack of genetic evidence and limited support from histopathology
No clear evidence of cutaneovisceral angiomatosis with thrombocytopenia
KRIT1 variant is more specific to cerebral cavernous malformations than CM-AVM syndrome
Lipolymphedema is a symptom rather than a primary diagnosis
Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome does not typically involve cerebral cavernous malformations
